raw.thesis: Narma is creating an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" to enable AI-first companies to seamlessly integrate and scale AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer with lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an "Intelligence Layer" or "Brain" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and identifies workflow "drift", and an "Execution Layer" (Agent Factory) that autonomously generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. This system does not create its own foundation models but rather leverages existing ones to focus on understanding and optimizing the "Work Graph" within an organization. It aims to address the challenges enterprises face in measuring AI savings, ensuring reliable ROI, and managing constant operational drift. Narma positions itself as a comprehensive solution that observes work, decides on AI interventions, and continuously builds agents for "Continuous AI lift." This venture is designed for growth companies, tackling a significant and frequent problem of demonstrating and scaling AI value in large organizations. It appears to be at the concept stage, leveraging existing AI capabilities to build a novel orchestration layer.
raw.what_makes_this_different: Narma's distinction lies in its holistic, three-layered approach to AI automation within enterprises, specifically focusing on the "Work Graph" and leveraging existing foundation models instead of building new ones. This allows them to focus on the orchestration and optimization of AI rather than foundational research.
raw.one_liner: An "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale.
raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. It features a three-layered architecture: an Observe Layer (lightweight desktop sensors), an Intelligence Layer (detects intent, business value, and drift), and an Execution Layer (Agent Factory for automated AI agent generation, deployment, and monitoring). It leverages existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify AI automation opportunities.
